en: The Philippine eagle builds large nests on tall dipterocarp trees to safely raise its chicks.
Male túngò frogs call from bamboo tubes to attract females during the rainy season.
Drinking clean, boiled water prevents infection by the microscopic cholera bacteria that causes severe diarrhea.
Mangrove roots trap sediment and protect Philippine coastlines from erosion during strong typhoons.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes and can rotate its head 180 degrees to spot insects.
Bats pollinate durian flowers at night, allowing the trees to produce fruit in tropical forests.
The human stomach produces strong hydrochloric acid to break down food and kill ingested bacteria.
Coral reefs in the Philippines support thousands of marine species by providing shelter and food.
The tropical pitcher plant traps and digests insects to absorb missing nutrients from poor soil.
Carabao wallow in mud to cool their bodies and protect their skin from biting insects.
Rice seeds germinate faster when soaked in water before being planted in flooded paddies.
Tiny air sacs called alveoli in the human lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.
